### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **74** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bf69cb41cc1f6351b0b0365ad7842a561611190f`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **19** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on objectstack-ai/objectstack#11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on objectstack-ai/objectstack#19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on objectstack-ai/objectstack#19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **184** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bf69cb41cc1f6351b0b0365ad7842a561611190f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c858927e8f8fd40a1d57c2d1239f1e78724decb4` — the merge of head `3bbf1a9817cfeb7b09d0a60b34eb78fbcf58747a` into base `bf69cb41cc1f6351b0b0365ad7842a561611190f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c858927e8f8fd40a1d57c2d1239f1e78724decb4 && git checkout c858927e8f8fd40a1d57c2d1239f1e78724decb4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bf69cb41cc1f6351b0b0365ad7842a561611190f 3bbf1a9817cfeb7b09d0a60b34eb78fbcf58747a && git checkout -B drift-repro bf69cb41cc1f6351b0b0365ad7842a561611190f && git merge --no-ff 3bbf1a9817cfeb7b09d0a60b34eb78fbcf58747a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bf69cb41cc1f6351b0b0365ad7842a561611190f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bf69cb41cc1f6351b0b0365ad7842a561611190f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1e43fdb1bc52ad397deba3e7735a27a55af3f73c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts + packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-docs.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts

PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#35564, card objectstack-ai/objectstack#35442. Read: the card body and its six comments, the PR body and its eleven files, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head (69 runs: 58 success, 11 skipped, none failed or pending; of the eleven required contexts ten are success and `Lint UI` is skipped, the diff holding no `ui/` path). The implementing files are named apart from the one `hits` file because the list's new jsdoc line describes them ("served at the door over the docs-audience gate") and the conformance test enforces it. The tests of the two new behaviours, the README, the changeset and the route-envelope row are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `MCP_DOOR_TOOL_NAMES` grows from 19 to 21 names. Right: it is what `wireBridgeTools` registers on a bridge carrying every optional member under every scope, and `mcp-file-tools.test.ts` (both members added to its bridge in this diff) holds the two equal. The list stays sorted and duplicate-free, which `platform-tool-names.test.ts` pins.
2. The `skill.tools[]` accept-set (`validateAiToolReferences`) does not move. Right: both names were already in `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES` through the `service-ai` group, so they resolved for every skill before, a skill with `mcpPrompt: false` included. No lint finding appears or disappears, so `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.
3. The spec's public surface: no export is added or removed; one exported constant's value grows. Right, and the api-surface gate inside `TypeScript Type Check` is green.
4. The door's `tools/list`: the pair is listed for an API key, a session or a `data:read` grant where the bridge carries both members. The runtime's HTTP bridge carries them where the protocol has `getMetaItems`; the stdio bridge carries neither. A widening, declared. Right.
5. `initialize`: the open server's default text gains one paragraph, under the same predicate that registers the pair (`packageDocToolsServed`). A host text and a configured `instructions` are served whole. Right.
6. `prompts/list`, which neither the PR body nor the changeset names: `registerSkillPrompts` offers a skill only where the connection serves every tool it binds (`skillBindingServed` over the server's registered tools). A skill binding either name was withheld on the HTTP door until now and is offered where the pair registers. Right by that rule. A skill written for the in-product tool's argument names meets the door's own input shape, and the door answers its alias refusal (`query` to `terms`), so the difference is loud.
7. Reuse of two names the cloud registry holds, the item the claim left unmeasured. Right: overlap is the list's stated design, and `platform-tool-names.test.ts` pins shared names. On the long-lived server a native name takes its name back from a bridged one (`yieldBridgedTool`), and the stdio bridge carries no doc member, so nothing moves there. On HTTP a host authoring registry that held either name would now meet the native registration and the SDK would throw for that request, which is the host duty `registerAuthoringTools` documents; the card's own reading of a cloud connection lists neither name. The cloud half of that conformance lives in the cloud repository.
8. `McpDataBridge` gains two optional members. Additive for every host. Right.
9. `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` declares `mcp-package-docs.ts` as `{ handBuilt: 0 }`. Right: the file builds no response, and the gate is green.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes — agreed. Two tools on the published door and two names on one exported list widen the surface; the line stands on the PR body and in the changeset, with no arm written, which the rule allows.

The changeset is `patch` on `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/spec`. It matches what the diff publishes: each of the three has published source in the diff, `Metadata-protocol: none` holds by ① item 2, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/lint` are read by the diff and not changed, so they are rightly absent. `Check Changeset` is success. Two of the changeset's sentences are the subject of S1 (the ranking) and S2 ("as the caller").

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report's `open_questions` is empty. Its flags, and the PR's acceptance notes:

- **No definition reader on a data-only connection** (carrier objectstack-ai/objectstack#34659 M-2, on hold). Answered. `definitionReaderServed` reads the request's own authoring registry under the predicate that registers it, so the rule never names a tool the connection does not list, and otherwise says the configuration was not checked. That is route A of claim amendment 7012002705. The card's second acceptance line (manual plus the `opportunity_approval` definition) can therefore be met only on a `metadata:write` connection whose registry lists `describe_metadata` or `get_metadata_item`.
- **stdio carries no doc member** ("carrier: none"). Answered. The README says so, and the list's jsdoc already qualifies itself as "on a bridge carrying every optional member". Whether stdio should carry the pair is a new card, the seat's call.
- **Book labels are served as authored.** Answered: an accepted deviation. The slug in the address is unaffected.
- **Host instructions win.** Escalated to the seat. The tree's own comments name the cloud build door as a host that injects `instructions` and `dataOnlyInstructions`, and a request answered by either text gets no rule appended. So card item 2 lands on open hosts only, and the environment the card's acceptance names receives the tools without the order text until that host adds it. Appending to a host text would break the rule that such a text is its author's whole. This needs a named carrier in the cloud repository before the card is read as accepted.
- **Live acceptance is after merge**, and the PR body says `Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#35442`, so the merge closes the card before its two acceptance lines have run. Escalated to the seat: reopen-or-carry is the seat's to decide.
- **S2 below names two ways to close it**, and choosing between them is a visibility decision: whose holdings a docs audience is asked about on a delegated token. Escalated to the seat; if no ruling of record covers it, it is the maintainer's.

SQL push-down: the diff adds no SQL and no id materialisation. The search is an in-app scan of the merged `/meta` doc list, and the helper's header gives the reason: no server-side doc search exists. Docs are metadata items the protocol's list read serves, not rows a driver query could filter, and ADR-0046 defers book-level search. No finding. The list read's own `names` narrowing, which `read_package_doc` does not use, is N3.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts` (the `hits` file).** Holds. The two entries are the names the `service-ai` group holds on `main`, and the new jsdoc clause is true of the tree: `registerPackageDocTools` registers them, and `mcp-package-docs.ts` reads `doc` and `book` through `createMetaListReadGate`. Tried against it: the lint accept-set (unchanged, ① item 2), a second registration under either name on each transport (① item 7), the stdio qualifier (the jsdoc's "every optional member"), and the conformance pin (both members added, so the equality is read from the registration site). The maintenance contract in the jsdoc is kept.

**`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`.** The registration gate agrees with its text: both members present, and either no scope list or one holding `data:read`, the predicate `initialize` reads too. Inputs are strict, with alias refusals. The read cut and its note agree with the changeset. Two sentences do not agree with the code: S1, and N1.

**`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`.** Holds against card item 2, sentence by sentence: a concept from the manual, and a general explanation labelled as one; a process from the manual and from its definition, the definition winning with the difference named; sources at the end. The rule is sent exactly where both tools register, and the reader it names is one the request registers.

**`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-docs.ts` and `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`.** Read for who can call and what an answer can show. Both lists pass the shared gate before anything else reads them, with no second rule. An unreadable gate input rejects; it is never an empty list. Results, their order, the cap and `truncated` are computed on the gated list only. A page that does not exist and a page the caller may not read answer the same `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` sentence. The ambiguity refusal names only packages of readable pages. The address is built from readable manuals alone, so no withheld manual's slug or label reaches a url, and its three segments are encoded. A name is compared by equality against the listed items: no path is read. The protocol is resolved for the request's environment as the bridge's other metadata reads resolve it. The domain opens with its anonymous deny, and the dispatcher's auth-policy gate sits above it. The home-manual pick agrees with the Console's (`homeBook`, `bookSlug`, `sortBooks` in `ui/apps/console/src/pages/book-nav.ts`). For a session or a key I found no page, package or manual served that the `/meta/doc` list would not serve the same caller. S2 is the one place the caller is not who the text says.

**`packages/mcp/src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts`.** Holds: the every-member bridge carries both new members, so the pin fails the day the list and the door differ.

S1 (should-fix) — the stated ranking is not the implemented one. The `search_package_docs` description, the jsdoc of `registerPackageDocTools` and the changeset say results are "ranked title, then heading, then text". `searchPackageDocs` sorts by `matched.length * 10 + rank`, where `rank` adds the place of every matched term (title 3, heading 2, text 1), and then by title. With two terms, a page holding both in its text scores 22 and outranks a page holding one in its title, 13. A title-and-text page ties a heading-and-heading page at 24, and the alphabet decides. The card's second question is the two-term case, and its pin (the opportunity manual first, both terms matched) passes on the rule the description leaves out. `matchedOn` reports the best place, which is not what the order used. The helper's header does state the term count, and its "then by where" is the sum, not the best place. Close it by stating the real order in the description, the jsdoc and the changeset, or by making the sort the stated one.

S2 (should-fix) — on an OAuth grant the audience is asked about the token's envelope, not the person. `mcp.ts` hands `packageDocsReadGate` the request's `executionContext`. For an OAuth token that is the agent envelope (`assemble-execution-context.ts`: `principalKind: 'agent'`, `permissions` replaced by the scope's ceiling set, the person kept as `onBehalfOf`), and the gate's `resolveAudienceCaller` asks `resolvePermissionSetNames` of it, which answers that ceiling set alone (`security-plugin-permission-sets.ts`). So a page only a `{ permissionSet }` manual claims is neither found nor read on a `data:read` token, whether or not the person holds the set. It fails closed, and default-audience manuals are unaffected. Three places in the diff say otherwise or leave it unsaid:
- The header says the module "hands the gate I/O only, as `mcp-authoring.ts` does for the open draft door's reads". That door hands the gate the person's own grants (`resolveHumanReader`: "never the agent envelope's"). On one connection `get_metadata_item` can then serve a page that `read_package_doc` answers as not found.
- The PR's control, "the holder finds and reads it", is pinned for a session-shaped context only.
- The registration gate reads `data:read`, the one grant this happens on, and no case drives an agent envelope through the bridge.

Close it one of two ways: ask the gate about the delegator's own holdings on an agent envelope, with a pin for that case; or keep the envelope, say so in the two descriptions, the changeset and the header, and pin the agent case as the stated limit. ③ escalates the choice.

N1 (nit) — both descriptions promise a url to cite. A page with no `_packageId` answers its name and title only (`addressOf`). The type declares `url` optional, so the type is right and the two sentences are wide. The Console's portal route would address such a page. Follow-up, or left.

N2 (nit) — `CONSOLE_BASE_PATH = '/_console'` is one more literal of the Console mount, beside the CLI's `CONSOLE_PATH` and the default of `uiBasePath`. A host that mounts the Console elsewhere answers a url that does not open. The card names the literal. Follow-up.

N3 (nit) — each call makes three list reads (the doc list, the book list inside the doc arm, the book list again), and `read_package_doc` reads every page's body to return one. The list read takes `names`, which the `/meta` list door hands down, and the gate's verdict for a page does not depend on which other pages are listed. No effect on the answer. Follow-up.

repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbUb7TcZK1XUAddUmQ

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3bbf1a9817cfeb7b09d0a60b34eb78fbcf58747a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts + packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-docs.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts

Delta d1 on PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#35564, card objectstack-ai/objectstack#35442, over the record in comment 7014988834 (head `1e43fdb1bc52ad397deba3e7735a27a55af3f73c`). Read: the one commit between the two heads, the PR body as it now stands, the dev delta (card comment 7016521809), the final-head comment 7016546315, and the check-runs on this head.

What moved: one commit, `3bbf1a9817`, whose only parent is the reviewed head. No merge of `main` is on the branch. It changes five files: the changeset, `packages/mcp/README.md`, `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-docs.ts` and its test. The `hits` file, `mcp-server-runtime.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `mcp-file-tools.test.ts`, the mcp tool-layer test and the route-envelope row are byte-identical to the reviewed head, so the first record's reading of them stands. `main` has moved 14 commits since the branch's merge base; none touches a path of this PR or a file the first record read to judge it, and GitHub reports the PR mergeable and clean.

Check-runs on this head: 73 runs, 59 success, 13 skipped, none failed, one cancelled. The cancelled one is a `PR-body guards` run the body edit superseded; its rerun is success. Of the eleven required contexts ten are success and `Lint UI` is skipped, the diff holding no `ui/` path.

### ① Derived judgments

1. No accept-set and no public-surface change in the delta. Right: the two tool names, their input schemas, the registration gate and `MCP_DOOR_TOOL_NAMES` are untouched. What changed on the door is two description strings.
2. The sort is unchanged; the texts moved to it. Right: `searchPackageDocs` still orders by `matched.length * 10 +` the place sum, then title.
3. Heading recognition changed with the parse. Right, and narrower in one way and wider in another, both stated below in ④: a bare `#` line no longer takes the next line as its text, and a `#` line counts at any indentation. Either can move a hit's `matchedOn`, its `heading` and a label-less page's title against the reviewed head. Nothing on `main` is compared, the feature being new.
4. The caller the gate is asked about is unchanged. Right: `mcp.ts` is untouched, and the texts now say whose holdings are read.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes — agreed, unchanged. The line stands on the PR body and in the changeset.

The changeset's frontmatter is untouched: `patch` on `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/spec`, which still matches what the diff publishes. `Metadata-protocol: none` still holds. Its three rewritten bullets agree with the tree: the order, the url "where the page has one", and the OAuth limit. `Check Changeset` is success on both of its runs.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev delta raises no open question. The three items the first record escalated:

- **Host instructions win.** Answered: the cloud carrier is filed as objectstack-ai/cloud#4905, nested under the card.
- **Live acceptance after merge.** Answered: the body now reads `Part of objectstack-ai/objectstack#35442`, and says the card stays open for the cloud carrier and the live acceptance. The card is open.
- **Whose holdings a docs audience is asked about on a delegated token.** Answered by the seat: the envelope is kept, which is the stricter of the two arms and widens nothing. The other arm, the delegating person's own sets, is carried as objectstack-ai/objectstack#35584 for its own decision.

SQL push-down: the delta adds no SQL and no id materialisation. No finding.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts` (the `hits` file).** Unchanged; holds as recorded.

**`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`.** Both descriptions and the `registerPackageDocTools` jsdoc now agree with the code, sentence by sentence: more of the terms first, then where the terms sit, then title; a url only where the page has one; and, on an OAuth connection, the connection's grant and not the person's own permission sets. The `McpDataBridge` jsdoc says the same of the principal.

**`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-docs.ts`.** The header states the order as it runs (the count, then the sum of title 3, heading 2, text 1, then title), names the caller as the request's execution context, says what that is on an OAuth grant and that it fails closed, and no longer claims parity with `mcp-authoring.ts`. The heading parse is now one pass over the page's lines (`headingsOf`), each line read by index (`headingTextOf`): one to six `#`, a space or tab on the same line, the text, a closing run dropped when a space precedes it. It agrees with its jsdoc and with the header's "line-based and linear". A line holding only `#` is no heading, and a heading can no longer take its text from the next line. Headings are computed once per page text and reused for the title, the heading match and the heading above a text match.

**`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-docs.test.ts`**, read as the pin of the stated limit. The agent case hands the dispatcher an envelope with `principalKind: 'agent'`, the person as `onBehalfOf` and a ceiling set as `permissions`, over a security fake that keeps the resolver's agent arm, and holds that the permission-set page is neither found nor read though the delegator holds the set. It would go red if the bridge handed the gate the delegator, which is the ablation the dev delta reports. Two more cases pin the parse: a very long heading line, and a bare `#` line followed by text.

**`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts`.** Unchanged; hold as recorded.

S1: closed
S2: closed
N1: closed

N2 and N3 are untouched and stay as nits, left or for a follow-up.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N4 (nit) — the agent case's ceiling set is spelled `mcp_agent_read`; the spec's constant is `mcp_agent_data_read` (`MCP_AGENT_PERMISSION_SET_READ`). The fake answers whatever the envelope carries, so the verdict does not depend on the spelling. Left, or the constant imported in a follow-up.

N5 (nit) — `headingTextOf` trims the line first, so a `#` line counts at any indentation, an indented code line included; the form it replaces counted only at column 0. It can move `matchedOn` and the title fallback for such a line and nothing else. Left.

N6 (nit) — the stated order (the count before the place sum) holds for up to six distinct terms, since one score carries both. The door caps `terms` at five; the bridge member itself sets no cap. Left.
